gap: No result ChatGPT got states what its own recommended '3 kWh battery + 400 W of solar' setup costs. ALLPOWERS sells exactly that as one kit (R3500, 3,168 Wh LiFePO4, + SP037 400 W) for $1,498 on its US store today. That is $1 less than the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2× 200 W kit ($1,499, 2,073.6 Wh) and less than half the $3,099 ChatGPT showed for the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 station with no panel.
standout_why: I compared against the three cited rival pages. solutionenergy.com/off-grid/cabins gives no product prices; it gives about 1 kWh a day and 2.5–3 kWh for two days, and names only a Renogy battery. Anker's setup guide lists F3800, F3000, C1000 and F2600 sizes with no prices. Anker's essentials checklist lists S2000 and C2000 Gen 2 with no prices. Our own Nov 3 page prices only kits of 2,073.6 Wh or less, and its Elite 200 V2 + 350 W price ($1,249) is now out of date ($1,449). None of them puts a dollar figure on a roughly 3 kWh + 400 W kit, or compares price per Wh across brands.
decides: This changes the pick. ChatGPT itself said a 2 kWh station 'generally won't reliably cover two full days' and recommended 3 kWh + 400 W, yet the card it showed was the 2,073.6 Wh Elite 200 V2. For the same $1,498–1,499 the shopper can buy 3,168 Wh + 400 W (ALLPOWERS R3500 kit), which is 1,094 Wh (53 %) more battery. Or for $1,598 they can get 3,168 Wh + 600 W, which covers ChatGPT's 350–600 W solar range. The Elite 200 V2 kits remain the 2 kWh choice for good sun. The R3500 is not in our catalog yet (ALLPOWERS is our CJ program), so it needs adding before the page can link it.
